label: prop:flavor-dressed-mass-from-substrate-split
title: Substrate-pure derivation of the dressed-quark mass splitting
html:
Let \mu \colon \mathbf{Flavor} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} be the flavor dressing functor. Let M_N be the average nucleon mass, and q = q_0 the substrate parameter. The down-up dressed mass splitting is exactly determined by the substrate flavor formula:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;=\;
  M_N \cdot \frac{(q - 1)^2 (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \cdot
  \frac{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;+\;
  O\!\left(\bigl(\Delta m / M_N\bigr)^2\right).

Dropping the O correction yields the leading-order substrate-pure form:

  \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}
  \;\approx\;
  \frac{M_N}{3} \cdot
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot
  \frac{1}{z_{\mathrm{mkv}}}.

The CODATA neutron-proton mass difference is no longer an input. The functor extracts the splitting purely from q_0 and the scale M_N. The individual masses \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} and \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} are then pinned by the baryon-content sum-rule.

Here z_{\mathrm{mkv}} = \sqrt q/(q+1) is the excised convention-C Markov weight, inherited from the pair-Skein formula. The statement is a convention-C result until that formula is re-derived under the canonical weight z = q^3/(q^2+1).

Conditional on two upstream results, neither yet formalised. The formal backing is a named accessor for a hypothesis carrying the substrate side (prop:flavor-split-substrate) together with the Skein side (lem:pair-skein-mass-formula), which is also where the O\!\left((\Delta m / M_N)^2\right) correction is absorbed. The equality above is asserted for a triple (\mu, M_N, q) carrying that hypothesis, not for an arbitrary one.
